bull_bear.body: Priority: repay INR 800cr high-cost Indian debt (10.5-11%) via proposed 10-year unsecured ECB at ~4%; free up collateral; fund working capital and India CapEx; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; debt reduction > CapEx > growth investment
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical uncertainty impacting pharma demand; regulatory delays in India/France; customer concentration in ADC and Vitamin D segments; FX volatility on CHF/INR (mitigated by natural hedge); pipeline attrition in late-phase projects; execution risk in India tech transfer
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly optimistic and confident; emphasized strategic alignment between India and Europe; highlighted successful execution on cost control, tech transfer, and ADC growth; cautious on near-term guidance but firm on 3-year targets; tone reinforced by Board approval of ECB refinancing
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The CHF 2.5M pension provision and INR 30M onerous contract charge are one-offs that masked underlying margin strength; India's operating margin historically was 35-40%, suggesting significant upside potential upon full capacity utilization; natural FX hedge exists as 90% of India revenue is in USD/EUR, offsetting ECB debt risk; Celonic partnership creates a unique end-to-end ADC offering not replicated by peers
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- integration: Single integrated CDMO partner spanning development (Switzerland) to commercial manufacturing (India) to finished formulations (France) — evidence: first API technology transfer agreed from Swiss operations to India, described as a milestone completed during the year.
- customer lock-in: Long-term co-investment partnership with a Japanese ADC innovator — evidence: second co-investment agreement entered into during the year for expansion of ADC capacity at Aarau and Hunzenschwil sites.
- licence/regulatory: Track record of passing major global regulatory inspections across sites — evidence: Shanghai facility cleared an NMPA inspection, Swiss sites cleared Swissmedic inspections, Netherlands facility received renewed GMP certificate from the Dutch authority (IGJ), and Naroda received US FDA regulatory clearance in August 2025, all within FY26.
- scale: Large multi-purpose manufacturing network across six countries — evidence: 23 multi-purpose manufacturing facilities supported by 32 R&D and HiPo laboratories, per the AR's facilities count.
- technology: Depth in high-potency and complex chemistry, including ADC/bioconjugation — evidence: Naroda site has zero product recalls and has successfully commercialized over 30 proprietary products; Aarau site fully integrated from drug-linker to filled vials at a single site with zero external tech transfers.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Export / geopolitical and trade-policy concentration — A substantial portion of revenue is export-derived; ongoing geopolitical tensions, disrupted trade routes, and evolving tariff and sanction regimes caused increased freight costs, longer transit times and heightened uncertainty across global markets during FY26.
- Related-party sales concentration — Sales to related parties were 68.11% of total sales in FY26 (73.20% in FY25), per the BRSR openness-of-business disclosure, indicating heavy reliance on intra-group transactions for revenue.
- Related-party loans and investment concentration — Loans & advances to related parties were 99.71% of total loans & advances, and investments in related parties were 99.44% of total investments, per the BRSR openness-of-business disclosure.
- New-site ramp-up risk (France) — The French entity's ramp-up has taken longer than expected because potential customers wanted to see a first late-phase or commercial project completed at the new site following ANSM regulatory approval, given the site's lack of track record with large Phase III or commercial molecules.
- Customer order loss at a manufacturing site (Bavla, India) — Bavla site operations were impacted by non-receipt of purchase orders from two large customers during FY26; the company states efforts are underway to recover this business.
- Industry patent-cliff and pricing pressure — Management's industry-overview discussion flags that several blockbuster oncology, immunology and metabolic drugs are expected to lose patent exclusivity through 2030, increasing competition from generics and biosimilars, alongside government drug-pricing negotiations and reimbursement reforms in developed markets.
- Rising competitive intensity in CDMO/API manufacturing — Management's industry overview cites rapid growth in pharmaceutical manufacturing capability in China and India, together with rising biosimilar penetration, as intensifying competitive pressure across multiple therapeutic categories.
- High employee attrition among permanent employees — Turnover rate for permanent employees rose to 43.82% in FY26 from 35.71% in FY25 and 21.00% in FY24, per the BRSR employee turnover disclosure.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: cautious on FY27, 3-year target intact; margin: targeting 25% EBITDA by FY28; order inflow: strong pipeline from tech transfer and ADC; capex/commissioning: no major CapEx except co-investments (100% funded by partners); digital transformation and SAP rollout ongoing
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: CHF 20-25M from Swiss API tech transfer to India; CHF 20-25M from new innovator API RFP; CHF 30-40M ADC linker-payload revenue expected in FY27-28; multiple late-phase projects with FDA inspection readiness
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Vertical integration: offering end-to-end drug substance-to-product services; India scaling: targeting INR 500cr+ revenue by FY28 via tech transfer and new RFPs; ADC expansion: multiple Phase 2/3 candidates in pipeline; Sprint initiative: capturing early-phase projects to feed future commercial volume; Celonic partnership: combined MAb-conjugation + drug product offering
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- SPRINT Initiative — internal programme aimed at winning more early-phase development projects (Smart and efficient, Proactive and agile, Regulatory compliant, Innovative science, No compromise on safety, Trusted partnership).
- Integrating the Swiss CDMO business with the Indian CDMO business, with a unified sales organisation offering end-to-end solutions to customers.
- Convert the first API technology transfer from Swiss operations to India into more transfers, using India's created capacity to drive incremental orders.
- Focus generic API business only on quaternary compounds and generic APIs meeting minimum margin criteria; discontinue or geography-restrict low-margin products.
- Expand the portfolio of contrast media products within generic APIs given perceived unmet demand.
- Explore backward integration of woolgrease saponification and Cholesterol manufacturing at the Bavla facility for cost advantage and supply-chain security.
- Reorganise the Dutch subsidiary's sales team with greater focus on higher-margin markets and products.
- Better utilise the Shanghai facility after receipt of local GMP certification to serve the entire Chinese API market; sales team focused on China has been strengthened.
- Continue investing in digital transformation initiatives for global integration and centralized processes.
- Strategic partnership between the Swiss subsidiary and Celonic AG for supply of monoclonal antibodies, extending the integrated ADC offering across the full chain (linker-payload synthesis through antibody conjugation to drug product formulation).
outlook.title: Strategy

outlook.body: Recent and planned manufacturing investment is concentrated on complex chemistries, high-potency compounds and advanced therapeutic platforms: expansion of sterile injectables capability in France (Saint-Beauzire, supporting formulation development and aseptic manufacturing, with a new GMP-qualified warehouse added to increase storage/batch capacity); strengthening of ADC and bioconjugation infrastructure in Switzerland (Aarau and Hunzenschwil sites, under a second co-investment agreement with a Japanese innovator to expand ADC capacity); capacity and technology upgrades at the Bavla and Naroda sites in India to improve scale, efficiency and process reliability; and continued investment in small-scale, high-value development capabilities across European sites. The company states that maintenance capital expenditure will continue at all global locations, and that digital transformation initiatives will keep being funded for global integration and centralized processes. At Shanghai, a new R&D centre and capacity for calcifediol are being planned. Management characterises major investments as largely complete, with the near-term task being to convert existing capacity (particularly in India) into orders and utilisation rather than to add further capacity.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Development activities in Switzerland saw a significant ramp-up in FY26 as the biotech funding environment improved after being slow in FY25.
- Dutch entity's continuous focus on cost improvement, particularly key raw material costs, resulted in cost advantages and helped secure more business.
- French entity's ramp-up was slow because customers wanted to see a first late-phase or commercial project at the new site following ANSM regulatory approval; pipeline of projects looks healthy with ramp-up expected over the next 18 months.
- Bavla site operations were impacted by non-receipt of purchase orders from two large customers in FY26; efforts underway to bring back that business and compensate via new business from closer Swiss-India collaboration.
- CDMO development revenue increased significantly relative to commercial revenue in FY26 on high supplies of late-phase projects and efforts to grow early-phase development work.
- ADC and bioconjugation programmes contributed approximately 25% of CDMO revenue in FY26, described as one of the most important growth platforms.
- Vitamin D Analogues and Cholesterol segment was the best-performing segment in FY26, a turnaround driven by high focus on the Vitamin D analogues sub-segment and better wool grease sourcing that lowered input costs.
- Geopolitical tensions, trade-route disruptions and evolving tariff/sanction regimes caused periodic logistics/supply-chain disruption in FY26, raising freight costs and transit times; a substantial portion of revenue is export-derived, making this an important area of focus, though the company states no material adverse impact on overall business performance to date.
- India is described as the key driver of the next phase of growth: capacity is largely already created, so the task ahead is to bring more orders to India, which will drive both revenue growth and margin improvement for the group as orders convert.
- Major investments are described as behind the company; the task now is to convert them into orders, utilisation and returns.
- More than 10 late-phase projects under execution, including process performance qualification (PPQ) campaigns.
- A base of more than 29 commercial products anchoring revenue generation.
- 10 molecules in late Phase III development pipeline.
- CHF 102 million new product development pipeline across ongoing customer programmes.
- Rising quotation rates and new project wins at Saint-Beauzire (France), with a growing pipeline of late-phase opportunities.
- Multiple tech transfer projects and new business opportunities being discussed and finalized as part of Swiss-India CDMO integration.
- Requests for Proposals increasing at the French facility, with potential new orders expected in the next 12-18 months.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Q4FY26 revenue surged 19% YoY to INR 851cr driven by strong CDMO and Vitamin D analog sales, with EBITDA margin expanding to 19.1% despite one-off pension and onerous contract provisions; key catalysts include tech transfer of CHF 20-25M Swiss API to India, ADC linker-payload growth (CHF 22M in FY26), and planned debt refinancing to cut interest costs by 700bps.

risks.note: A substantial portion of revenue is export-derived; ongoing geopolitical tensions, disrupted trade routes, and evolving tariff and sanction regimes caused increased freight costs, longer transit times and heightened uncertainty across global markets during FY26.
Sales to related parties were 68.11% of total sales in FY26 (73.20% in FY25), per the BRSR openness-of-business disclosure, indicating heavy reliance on intra-group transactions for revenue.
Loans & advances to related parties were 99.71% of total loans & advances, and investments in related parties were 99.44% of total investments, per the BRSR openness-of-business disclosure.

The French entity's ramp-up has taken longer than expected because potential customers wanted to see a first late-phase or commercial project completed at the new site following ANSM regulatory approval, given the site's lack of track record with large Phase III or commercial molecules.

risks.risk: Customer order loss at a manufacturing site (Bavla, India)
risks.note: Bavla site operations were impacted by non-receipt of purchase orders from two large customers during FY26; the company states efforts are underway to recover this business.

Management's industry-overview discussion flags that several blockbuster oncology, immunology and metabolic drugs are expected to lose patent exclusivity through 2030, increasing competition from generics and biosimilars, alongside government drug-pricing negotiations and reimbursement reforms in developed markets.

risks.risk: Rising competitive intensity in CDMO/API manufacturing
risks.note: Management's industry overview cites rapid growth in pharmaceutical manufacturing capability in China and India, together with rising biosimilar penetration, as intensifying competitive pressure across multiple therapeutic categories.

risks.risk: High employee attrition among permanent employees
risks.note: Turnover rate for permanent employees rose to 43.82% in FY26 from 35.71% in FY25 and 21.00% in FY24, per the BRSR employee turnover disclosure.

one-line thesis: Q4FY26 revenue surged 19% YoY to INR 851cr driven by strong CDMO and Vitamin D analog sales, with EBITDA margin expanding to 19.1% despite one-off pension and onerous contract provisions; key catalysts include tech transfer of CHF 20-25M Swiss API to India, ADC linker-payload growth (CHF 22M in FY26), and planned debt refinancing to cut interest costs by 700bps.
financial scorecard: revenue: +19% YoY to INR 851cr; EBITDA/margin: +19.1% (19.3% FY26); PAT (rptd): INR 21.7cr (Q4); PAT (normalized): ~INR 35cr (ex-CHF 2.5M pension provision + INR 30cr onerous contract charge); order book: CHF 40-50M from tech transfer + ADC projects (unconfirmed); net debt: -CHF 11M YoY to CHF 146.8M (ex-lease)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Development activities in Switzerland saw a significant ramp-up in FY26 as the biotech funding environment improved after being slow in FY25.
- Dutch entity's continuous focus on cost improvement, particularly key raw material costs, resulted in cost advantages and helped secure more business.
- French entity's ramp-up was slow because customers wanted to see a first late-phase or commercial project at the new site following ANSM regulatory approval; pipeline of projects looks healthy with ramp-up expected over the next 18 months.
- Bavla site operations were impacted by non-receipt of purchase orders from two large customers in FY26; efforts underway to bring back that business and compensate via new business from closer Swiss-India collaboration.
- CDMO development revenue increased significantly relative to commercial revenue in FY26 on high supplies of late-phase projects and efforts to grow early-phase development work.
- ADC and bioconjugation programmes contributed approximately 25% of CDMO revenue in FY26, described as one of the most important growth platforms.
- Vitamin D Analogues and Cholesterol segment was the best-performing segment in FY26, a turnaround driven by high focus on the Vitamin D analogues sub-segment and better wool grease sourcing that lowered input costs.
- Geopolitical tensions, trade-route disruptions and evolving tariff/sanction regimes caused periodic logistics/supply-chain disruption in FY26, raising freight costs and transit times; a substantial portion of revenue is export-derived, making this an important area of focus, though the company states no material adverse impact on overall business performance to date.
- India is described as the key driver of the next phase of growth: capacity is largely already created, so the task ahead is to bring more orders to India, which will drive both revenue growth and margin improvement for the group as orders convert.
- Major investments are described as behind the company; the task now is to convert them into orders, utilisation and returns.
- More than 10 late-phase projects under execution, including process performance qualification (PPQ) campaigns.
- A base of more than 29 commercial products anchoring revenue generation.
- 10 molecules in late Phase III development pipeline.
- CHF 102 million new product development pipeline across ongoing customer programmes.
- Rising quotation rates and new project wins at Saint-Beauzire (France), with a growing pipeline of late-phase opportunities.
- Multiple tech transfer projects and new business opportunities being discussed and finalized as part of Swiss-India CDMO integration.
- Requests for Proposals increasing at the French facility, with potential new orders expected in the next 12-18 months.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: CDMO margin dip in Q4 due to lower high-margin Phase 3 deliveries; Vitamin D analogs margin improved via wool grease supplier diversification and cost optimization; overall EBITDA margin expanded 200bps to 19.3% in FY26; ADC margins >2x consolidated average (estimated 40-50%); pension provision (CHF 2.5M) and onerous contract charge (INR 30cr) distorted Q4 EBITDA

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Priority: repay INR 800cr high-cost Indian debt (10.5-11%) via proposed 10-year unsecured ECB at ~4%; free up collateral; fund working capital and India CapEx; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; debt reduction > CapEx > growth investment

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Recent and planned manufacturing investment is concentrated on complex chemistries, high-potency compounds and advanced therapeutic platforms: expansion of sterile injectables capability in France (Saint-Beauzire, supporting formulation development and aseptic manufacturing, with a new GMP-qualified warehouse added to increase storage/batch capacity); strengthening of ADC and bioconjugation infrastructure in Switzerland (Aarau and Hunzenschwil sites, under a second co-investment agreement with a Japanese innovator to expand ADC capacity); capacity and technology upgrades at the Bavla and Naroda sites in India to improve scale, efficiency and process reliability; and continued investment in small-scale, high-value development capabilities across European sites. The company states that maintenance capital expenditure will continue at all global locations, and that digital transformation initiatives will keep being funded for global integration and centralized processes. At Shanghai, a new R&D centre and capacity for calcifediol are being planned. Management characterises major investments as largely complete, with the near-term task being to convert existing capacity (particularly in India) into orders and utilisation rather than to add further capacity.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly optimistic and confident; emphasized strategic alignment between India and Europe; highlighted successful execution on cost control, tech transfer, and ADC growth; cautious on near-term guidance but firm on 3-year targets; tone reinforced by Board approval of ECB refinancing

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- integration: Single integrated CDMO partner spanning development (Switzerland) to commercial manufacturing (India) to finished formulations (France) — evidence: first API technology transfer agreed from Swiss operations to India, described as a milestone completed during the year.
- customer lock-in: Long-term co-investment partnership with a Japanese ADC innovator — evidence: second co-investment agreement entered into during the year for expansion of ADC capacity at Aarau and Hunzenschwil sites.
- licence/regulatory: Track record of passing major global regulatory inspections across sites — evidence: Shanghai facility cleared an NMPA inspection, Swiss sites cleared Swissmedic inspections, Netherlands facility received renewed GMP certificate from the Dutch authority (IGJ), and Naroda received US FDA regulatory clearance in August 2025, all within FY26.
- scale: Large multi-purpose manufacturing network across six countries — evidence: 23 multi-purpose manufacturing facilities supported by 32 R&D and HiPo laboratories, per the AR's facilities count.
- technology: Depth in high-potency and complex chemistry, including ADC/bioconjugation — evidence: Naroda site has zero product recalls and has successfully commercialized over 30 proprietary products; Aarau site fully integrated from drug-linker to filled vials at a single site with zero external tech transfers.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical uncertainty impacting pharma demand; regulatory delays in India/France; customer concentration in ADC and Vitamin D segments; FX volatility on CHF/INR (mitigated by natural hedge); pipeline attrition in late-phase projects; execution risk in India tech transfer

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The CHF 2.5M pension provision and INR 30M onerous contract charge are one-offs that masked underlying margin strength; India's operating margin historically was 35-40%, suggesting significant upside potential upon full capacity utilization; natural FX hedge exists as 90% of India revenue is in USD/EUR, offsetting ECB debt risk; Celonic partnership creates a unique end-to-end ADC offering not replicated by peers

strategy.title: Strategy
strategy.body:
- SPRINT Initiative — internal programme aimed at winning more early-phase development projects (Smart and efficient, Proactive and agile, Regulatory compliant, Innovative science, No compromise on safety, Trusted partnership).
- Integrating the Swiss CDMO business with the Indian CDMO business, with a unified sales organisation offering end-to-end solutions to customers.
- Convert the first API technology transfer from Swiss operations to India into more transfers, using India's created capacity to drive incremental orders.
- Focus generic API business only on quaternary compounds and generic APIs meeting minimum margin criteria; discontinue or geography-restrict low-margin products.
- Expand the portfolio of contrast media products within generic APIs given perceived unmet demand.
- Explore backward integration of woolgrease saponification and Cholesterol manufacturing at the Bavla facility for cost advantage and supply-chain security.
- Reorganise the Dutch subsidiary's sales team with greater focus on higher-margin markets and products.
- Better utilise the Shanghai facility after receipt of local GMP certification to serve the entire Chinese API market; sales team focused on China has been strengthened.
- Continue investing in digital transformation initiatives for global integration and centralized processes.
- Strategic partnership between the Swiss subsidiary and Celonic AG for supply of monoclonal antibodies, extending the integrated ADC offering across the full chain (linker-payload synthesis through antibody conjugation to drug product formulation).

one-line thesis: Q4FY26 revenue surged 19% YoY to INR 851cr driven by strong CDMO and Vitamin D analog sales, with EBITDA margin expanding to 19.1% despite one-off pension and onerous contract provisions; key catalysts include tech transfer of CHF 20-25M Swiss API to India, ADC linker-payload growth (CHF 22M in FY26), and planned debt refinancing to cut interest costs by 700bps.
financial scorecard: revenue: +19% YoY to INR 851cr; EBITDA/margin: +19.1% (19.3% FY26); PAT (rptd): INR 21.7cr (Q4); PAT (normalized): ~INR 35cr (ex-CHF 2.5M pension provision + INR 30cr onerous contract charge); order book: CHF 40-50M from tech transfer + ADC projects (unconfirmed); net debt: -CHF 11M YoY to CHF 146.8M (ex-lease)
guidance: revenue growth: cautious on FY27, 3-year target intact; margin: targeting 25% EBITDA by FY28; order inflow: strong pipeline from tech transfer and ADC; capex/commissioning: no major CapEx except co-investments (100% funded by partners); digital transformation and SAP rollout ongoing
order book & pipeline: CHF 20-25M from Swiss API tech transfer to India; CHF 20-25M from new innovator API RFP; CHF 30-40M ADC linker-payload revenue expected in FY27-28; multiple late-phase projects with FDA inspection readiness

growth verticals / optionality: Vertical integration: offering end-to-end drug substance-to-product services; India scaling: targeting INR 500cr+ revenue by FY28 via tech transfer and new RFPs; ADC expansion: multiple Phase 2/3 candidates in pipeline; Sprint initiative: capturing early-phase projects to feed future commercial volume; Celonic partnership: combined MAb-conjugation + drug product offering
margins & cost dynamics: CDMO margin dip in Q4 due to lower high-margin Phase 3 deliveries; Vitamin D analogs margin improved via wool grease supplier diversification and cost optimization; overall EBITDA margin expanded 200bps to 19.3% in FY26; ADC margins >2x consolidated average (estimated 40-50%); pension provision (CHF 2.5M) and onerous contract charge (INR 30cr) distorted Q4 EBITDA
capex / expansion: CHF 22.4M in FY26; no major hard asset CapEx planned; co-investments with Japanese innovator fully funded by partner; digital CapEx: SAP implementation, AI-driven lab systems, process automation

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.

hero.oneLiner: A globally integrated Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisation (CDMO) spanning process development in Switzerland, large-scale manufacturing in India, and finished parenteral formulations from France, with 23 multi-purpose manufacturing facilities across 6 countries.
